title: Turn a raw screen recording into a polished demo
description: Record locally, reconstruct input events on Wayland, and export the same polished composition shown in the editor.

image.alt: A ScreenPolish export with the recorded application framed on a gradient background

screenshots.alt: ScreenPolish capture workspace showing the recording library and capture sources

problem: Software demos usually need a second editing pass for framing, zooms, cursor cleanup, and exports. On Wayland, an application also cannot rely on the global input hooks used by conventional recorders.
solution: ScreenPolish records the screen locally, reconstructs pointer motion from Hyprland IPC and clicks from evdev, and applies every visual effect through one pure renderer shared by preview and export.
workflow: Capture video through xdg-desktop-portal and PipeWire while recording pointer motion and click events without opening keyboard devices.
Store the capture and event timeline together so every edit remains deterministic.
Render zooms, cursor motion, click ripples, framing, and optional webcam composition from the same frame-and-events function.
Export MP4 or GIF in landscape, square, or vertical formats from the composition already approved in preview.
limitations: The macOS build is still early.
The Linux input path is tailored to Hyprland for pointer coordinates and uses evdev only for click events.
Source is private; the case study documents behavior and architecture without publishing the repository.

title: Run a daily content workflow with agents and owner review
description: Coordinate research, drafting, verification, and scheduling in a local-first newsroom for one X account.

image.alt: Hermes X Mission Control Today view with editorial agents, queues, and the daily content plan

screenshots.alt: Hermes X Mission Control Today view

problem: Running an active account requires a repeatable cycle of research, drafting, checking, scheduling, and review. Loose documents make handoffs and editorial accountability hard to see.
solution: Mission Control turns the process into a thirteen-screen editorial workspace. Named agent profiles move work through explicit queues with receipts, while publication remains behind owner review.
workflow: Run the scheduled 8am audit to collect the day's research and content needs.
Move candidate ideas through research, drafting, and verification queues with a record of each handoff.
Review the proposed post, source material, and checks in one owner-facing workspace.
Approve the final item for the calendar and track published work and analytics.
limitations: The product currently serves one account and one owner.
Nothing publishes without explicit owner review.
Source is private; this entry documents the working system without exposing the repository.

title: Create a complete specialist bot from one sentence
description: Generate identity, memory, tools, routines, and a managed gateway while rolling back incomplete provisioning.

image.alt: Hermes Bot Forge turning a one-sentence request into a complete bot named Inkwell

screenshots.alt: Hermes Bot Forge working bot demonstration

problem: A useful specialist agent needs more than a prompt: it needs an identity, durable memory, tools, skills, routines, and a service that starts reliably. Manual setup leaves many chances for a half-configured bot.
solution: Bot Forge converts one sentence into a complete Hermes Agent bot, verifies every provisioning step, and removes the partial bot if any step fails.
workflow: Interpret the requested role and generate a name, face, purpose-built SOUL.md, and initial memory.
Select and configure the tools, skills, and optional scheduled routines needed for the role.
Create and verify the gateway service that keeps the bot available after login.
Commit the bot only after every step passes; otherwise roll the entire provisioning attempt back.
limitations: Generated bots still need a clear job and reviewed permissions.
A provisioning rollback protects configuration integrity but cannot guarantee that a chosen external integration is available.
Gateway setup depends on the host platform's service behavior.

title: Reach specialist agents without leaving the workspace
description: Chat with any configured Hermes profile in a floating or docked panel and assign only selected messages to Kanban.

image.alt: Hermes Agent Dock floating specialist chat panel

screenshots.alt: Agent Dock floating specialist chat card
Agent Dock attached to the bottom of the Hermes Desktop workspace

problem: When the main orchestrator is occupied, specialist profiles are difficult to reach from the desktop. Mixing every conversation with task tracking also creates noise and accidental work items.
solution: Agent Dock exposes the profiles Hermes already knows in a direct chat panel that can float or attach to the workspace. Chat remains chat until the user explicitly assigns a message to Kanban.
workflow: Read the local Hermes profile inventory and present available specialists.
Open a direct conversation while other profile jobs continue independently.
Keep the panel floating or dock it into the workspace and remember that layout choice.
Assign a message to Kanban only when it should become tracked work.
limitations: The dock requires an existing Hermes Desktop installation and configured profiles.
Kanban assignment is intentionally explicit, so ordinary chat is not automatically converted into tasks.
The installer and release behavior must track changes in Hermes Desktop.

title: Browse skills, plugins, and community workflows in one place
description: A profile-aware Hermes Desktop library with compact cards, category and author filters, and reviewed import paths.

image.alt: Hermes Skills Library use-case browser with category filters and compact story cards

screenshots.alt: Use cases from the Nous documentation inside Hermes Skills Library

problem: Hermes capabilities and community workflows live across catalogs, documentation, and attributed source stories. Builders need a fast way to find a relevant capability without losing provenance or installing into the wrong profile.
solution: The library adds one Hermes Desktop surface for skills, plugins, and an attributed snapshot of official community stories, with search, source filters, category and author browsing, and explicit destination profiles.
workflow: Load the reviewed skills and plugin catalogs plus the bundled official use-case snapshot.
Search or filter by source, category, author, and active Agent profile.
Open a compact card to inspect attribution, requirements, and available details before taking action.
Import through Hermes' existing scanning and installation paths while preserving profile selection and disable states.

outcomes.label: attributed community stories in the bundled snapshot

limitations: The early community release is verified on Linux; macOS and Windows are not yet verified.
Hermes internal Python and Desktop SDK APIs can change between releases.
Inferred categories and brief summaries can require editorial correction; source attribution is preserved for review.

title: Browse local Git repositories as a working 3D bookshelf
description: Turn configured folders into shelves and repositories into books that expose status, history, and safe local actions.

image.alt: Repo Shelf interface showing Git repositories as books in a 3D bookcase

screenshots.alt: Repo Shelf 3D bookcase and repository search controls

problem: A large collection of local repositories is difficult to scan as folders alone. Important signals such as activity, size, language, stars, and uncommitted changes are scattered across tools.
solution: Repo Shelf maps configured root folders to shelves and Git repositories to books. Visual properties communicate repository state, while opening a book exposes details and guarded local actions.
workflow: Scan configured root folders one level deep and enrich repositories with local Git and optional GitHub CLI metadata.
Derive book height, thickness, color, bands, tabs, and stamps from repository facts.
Search, orbit, zoom, or open a book to inspect README, commits, issues, pull requests, files, and branches.
Run guarded local actions such as moving, renaming, cloning, or opening a repository, with conflicts and uncommitted work surfaced first.
limitations: Local operation requires Node 24 and Git; GitHub enrichment requires an authenticated GitHub CLI.
Repository actions have real filesystem effects and therefore use confirmations and conflict checks.
The 3D interface is intentionally experimental and can demand more graphics performance than a conventional list.
